races.note: The top two finishers from the Nov 3, 2026 count. Everyone else in this race is coming.

cands.name: Kanika Brown
cands.bio: Democratic member of the North Carolina House for District 71 (part of Forsyth County, Winston-Salem) since January 2023. Describes herself as a community activist and small business owner. Former substitute teacher and teacher's aide. Lost the 2020 Democratic primary, then won the seat in 2022.

endorsements.text: North Carolina AFL-CIO (stated on her campaign platform page).
Listed in Ballotpedia's 2026 endorsements and voter guide recommendations: Unburdening The Ballot: Voting Made Easy (Sway voting group by Tevin (Momala) Davis).

cands.gaps: We couldn't find where she was born or raised, or when she moved to North Carolina. We found no specific bills she sponsored, since the sponsored-legislation list did not display. Her campaign site mentions bills on local government, fair maps, nonprofits, workforce and environmental justice without naming them. We found no stated positions or documented actions from her on data centers, homestead property taxes, limits on investor or foreign land buyers, growth and land protection, H-1B or immigration enforcement, police pay, gun laws, or school vouchers. Her campaign site calls for more affordable housing built with developers and local governments, but it is not specific enough to count as a position on growth limits. Her site also calls her campaign "unbossed, unbought," but it does not state a specific pledge about refusing particular donors. She did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate surveys. We found no controversies or foreign ties in the pages reviewed.

cands.name: Mathew Mena
cands.bio: Mathew Mena was the Green Party candidate for North Carolina House District 71 in 2026. He lost the general election to incumbent Democrat Kanika Brown. The sources found give no other information about his background.
cands.gaps: We couldn't find Mathew Mena's birthplace, where he grew up, when he came to North Carolina, or his occupation and work history. He did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate survey, and no campaign website, interviews or questionnaires were available, so we have no record of his stated positions on data centers, property taxes, development, immigration, policing, guns, abortion or schools. Ballotpedia lists no endorsements for him. He has not held office, so there is no record of official actions.
